source.title: Quantifying Depth Sufficiency in Residual Neural Networks: A First-Order Criterion
source.authors: Ze-Yu Liu; Jin-Hao Zhang; Yun-Quan Zhang; Guang-Ming Tan; Xiang Gao; Fang-Min Liu; Da-Ning Cheng

record.file_problem: Supplied text is the full paper. It contains minor transcription/formatting errors in the experimental discussion, but the relevant results and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Measures activation-gradient signals across depth and tests function-preserving residual insertion and continued training, bearing conceptually on depth and training behavior. It does not test the claim's random-initialization classification-error sweep.
record.gate_note: Results include fixed-sample activation-gradient norms across model depths, converged growth-versus-scratch loss comparisons, and immediate loss changes after gradient-matched insertions. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows. The growth-versus-scratch comparison concerns converged loss, not zero training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study measures remaining local value of residual insertion, activation-gradient signals, and growth-versus-scratch losses. These do not test any stated version: in particular, depth saturation in residual networks does not establish depth-related training degradation or its prevention by identity shortcuts. No plain-network comparison is provided.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate with qualifications: under the stated regularity and fixed zero-state first-order protocol, tangent-space projection gives an exact local saturation criterion. Raw activation-gradient norms are conservative diagnostics, becoming exact under residual-signal realizability. Experiments report low-signal regimes with depth and competitive converged losses from function-preserving growth. These conclusions concern local residual-growth value, not the six claim versions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fixed-function residual insertion, activation-gradient measurement, and continued optimization; does not reproduce the original depth-degradation or shortcut-versus-plain training-error comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported signal and marginal performance improvement vary with depth and model family. The authors note ImageNet-100 is less monotone at intermediate depths and Pythia varies in architecture as well as depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-gradient diagnostics generally decline toward low-signal plateaus with depth. Pythia comparisons also vary other architectural dimensions. Extended-depth residual models retain low reported scores while training losses decrease and test losses fluctuate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under a specified residual-growth protocol, small activation-gradient signals may conservatively indicate little remaining empirical first-order value of additional residual depth; numerical certification requires resolving the diagnostic's normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Growth reaches training losses below Scratch for ResNet-10, ResNet-11, and ResNet-13 and slightly above Scratch for ResNet-12; test losses are lower for Growth in all four configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Function-preserving residual growth can reach competitive converged losses relative to scratch training at the same final CIFAR-10 architecture; this comparison does not establish training efficiency.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitting an inserted residual block to a negative activation-gradient target produces immediate training-loss reductions of 0.0007, 0.0004, 0.0002, and 0.0002; held-out changes are within reported uncertainty.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A deliberately gradient-matched residual insertion can yield a small immediate empirical loss reduction without subsequent task-loss training.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical result equates local first-order improvability with a nonzero activation-gradient projection onto the fixed residual tangent space, under regularity and zero-state descent-compatible updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-tangent projection characterizes local first-order saturation relative to a fixed insertion protocol; replacing it with raw activation gradients requires residual-signal realizability for equivalence.

record.problems: No direct training classification-error results; no plain-network control or shortcut ablation; activation-gradient realizability is not verified, so AGmax is an upper bound on projected growth value; no uncertainty reported for most depth-sweep values; Pythia is not a controlled depth-only comparison; extended-depth test losses fluctuate; growth-versus-scratch comparison is not compute-matched; immediate insertion is gradient-matched using the training sample.
record.rows_left_out: None. All individually reported text/table results relevant to the tested depth and residual-growth behavior are included. Figure curves are described qualitatively rather than read for unreported precise values.

untested.parts: Training classification-error rates across model sizes and label corruption are not reported. Small cross-entropy losses are reported, but no classification-error comparison tests the specified claim.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, or extra-student-neuron comparison.
No plain-network depth-degradation experiment, matched identity-shortcut comparison, longer-training control, very deep plain tanh experiment, or normalization-free residual-training test.

No activation-matched initialization comparison measuring learning speed or trainable depth, Gaussian-versus-orthogonal comparison, or orthogonal convolution experiment. Growth versus Scratch measures final losses.
No initial stability-limit comparison, catapult loss trajectory, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability measurement, or threshold-related divergence experiment.
No batch-normalization ablation measuring training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and no Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V3 limits_scope verdict: an untested plain-versus-shortcut training-error contrast is not a scope limitation. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied versions; this does not dispute the reported numerical changes. Appendix B.1's distinction between logged batch-level norms and theoretical sample-normalized scores also prevents treating the reported nonzero scores as calibrated projected-growth bounds without clarification.

versions.untested_parts: No systematic comparison of training classification error for sufficiently large versus smaller randomly initialized convolutional networks, and no corrupted-label or random-label experiments.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments, spurious-minimum rates, or student-width comparison.

Does not compare plain versus identity-shortcut networks or test whether shortcuts prevent depth-related training error. Reports ResNet depth sweeps and residual growth, but no plain-network ablation.
No comparison of initialization schemes or tests of initialization effects on learning speed or trainable depth.
No above-stability learning-rate or sharpness experiments.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization speed or learning-rate-tolerance comparison; no Fixup experiment.

rows.subject: ResNet (CIFAR-10)
rows.size_stated: ResNet-8 backbone; base channels 16; N=1,...,100 added blocks; 3+N residual blocks total
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; well-trained
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum sample-wise activation-gradient norm across depth during depth sweep.

conditions.value: SGD with momentum; initial learning rate 0.1, multiplied by 0.1 after epochs 100 and 150
300 epochs maximum; early stopping enabled only after at least 180 epochs

rows.measure: AGmax, maximum sample-wise activation-gradient norm across admissible residual insertion locations
rows.value: Figure 1 shows rapid decrease at shallow and intermediate depths followed by a stable low-signal regime. At approximately 16 residual structures, AGmax = 0.00381.
rows.locator: Experiments, Activation-Gradient Norms Across Model Depth; Figure 1; Appendix B.2 and Table 5
rows.note: The text describes the trend and gives the approximate depth and score, but does not report a training classification-error curve. This is evidence about gradient signal and task-loss improvement, not the claim's zero-error criterion.
rows.check: Activation-gradient magnitude does not measure V3's training-error effect. Appendix B.1 says the logged diagnostic averages whole-batch gradient norms; its nonzero scale need not equal the sample-normalized AGmax defined in the main text.

rows.subject: ResNet (ImageNet-100)

rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; well-trained

conditions.value: initial sweep N in {1,5,9,...,49}; extended configurations ResNet-256/257/258

rows.measure: AGmax, maximum sample-wise activation-gradient norm across admissible residual insertion locations
rows.value: Initial sweep: overall AGmax envelope decreases and reaches its minimum at the largest evaluated depth; intermediate depths are less monotone. Extended ResNet-256/257/258 AGmax scores are 0.0020/0.0018/0.0011.
rows.locator: Experiments, Activation-Gradient Norms Across Model Depth; Figure 1; Extended-depth evaluation; Appendix B.3

Extended-depth scores are duplicated in R6; the text calls these residual-structure counts, not standard ResNet layer counts.

rows.subject: GPT-2-style models
rows.size_stated: baseline L=12 decoder blocks; controlled depth sweep and extended configurations with 700/701/702 residual structures
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on FineWeb-Edu
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum sample-wise activation-gradient norm across depth during depth sweep.

conditions.value: controlled decoder-block sweep; extended configurations 700/701/702 residual structures
up to five rounds initially; selected checkpoints continued to ten rounds

rows.measure: AGmax, maximum sample-wise activation-gradient norm across admissible residual insertion locations
rows.value: Controlled sweep: AGmax decreases rapidly at shallow and intermediate depths, then changes modestly in a stable low-signal regime. Extended configurations 700/701/702 have AGmax scores 0.0033/0.0029/0.0022.
rows.locator: Experiments, Activation-Gradient Norms Across Model Depth; Figure 1; Extended-depth evaluation; Appendix B.4 and Table 6
rows.note: The GPT-2 comparison is a language-modeling depth sweep, not a CIFAR classification-error experiment. Training classification error is not measured.
rows.check: Language-model activation-gradient norms do not measure V3's convolutional training-error contrast. Appendix B.1 distinguishes logged batch norms from theoretical AGmax. Documented five- or ten-round caps do not establish convergence for every model.

rows.subject: Pythia checkpoints
rows.size_stated: six deduplicated pretrained model configurations spanning a range of model sizes; individual names and sizes not stated
rows.stage_stated: official step143000 checkpoints continued-pretrained on FineWeb-Edu; frozen during activation-gradient measurement
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation-gradient norms across model depth and continued-pretraining checkpoints.
rows.measure: AGmax, maximum sample-wise activation-gradient norm across admissible residual insertion locations
rows.value: The text describes a sharper transition to a stable low-signal regime; at approximately 33 residual structures, AGmax = 0.0008.
rows.locator: Experiments, Activation-Gradient Norms Across Model Depth; Figure 1; Appendix B.5
rows.note: The authors caution that Pythia configurations vary in architectural dimensions in addition to depth, so these are cross-model rather than controlled depth-only results. No classification error is measured.
rows.check: Cross-model activation-gradient measurements do not test any version. Architectural dimensions vary alongside depth, and Appendix B.1 distinguishes the logged batch-level diagnostic from theoretical AGmax.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reported depth sweeps, residual growth, and gradient-matched insertion experiments
reader_labels.reason: The study reports low gradient-signal plateaus with depth and competitive converged loss after function-preserving growth, but it does not measure the version's plain-versus-shortcut training-error contrast; its immediate insertion losses are small and deliberately gradient-matched (R1-R23).
